gaps.sentence: The ___ (SURVIVE) of the species is under threat.
gaps.explanation: The noun from SURVIVE is 'survival'; a survivor is a person.

gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: In my opinion, that restaurant is ___ — the food is nothing special (RATE).
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing special' shows the restaurant is praised too much: overrated (over- + rated).

gaps.hint: subject of the sentence: noun needed (-ness becomes -ty here)
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: Honesty. The spelling changes -ness to -ty; 'honestness' is not a word.

gaps.sentence: The ___ between rich and poor is widening (DIVIDE).
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: division (-sion). 'Divisive' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: He denied all knowledge of the ___ (APPEAR) of the documents.
gaps.explanation: The documents vanished, so the negative noun 'disappearance' is needed; 'appearance' means coming into view.

gaps.sentence: He felt he was ___ for the work he did, so he asked for a raise (PAY).
gaps.hint: paid too little — he wants a raise (under-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix under- means too little: underpaid means paid less than deserved, which explains asking for a raise.
